subject: Next steps: Sienna Health pilot — evaluation datasets & scoring
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Parker <luke.parker@siennahealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@siennahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-18T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Next steps: Sienna Health pilot — evaluation datasets & scoring

Hi Luke / Priya — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum on the pilot and get a representative benchmark run on Redwood.

Recap from call:
- Goal: run a 1–2k example pilot eval to validate retrieval + generative summarization quality for clinical note condensation and triage suggestions.
- Priority metrics you care about: clinical accuracy (no introduced hallucinations), coverage of critical fields, and latency targets (~<600ms per request at 95p for interactive workflows).

What I attached: si_eval_sample.jsonl (sample format, 100 records) — use this to mirror your export.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Share a ~1k de‑identified sample in the attached JSONL schema (or confirm you can export the fields). If you need a de‑id checklist I can share one.
2) Confirm whether you want strict exact-match scoring on key fields (diagnosis codes / medication mentions) vs. fuzzy / semantic scoring for summaries.
3) Let us know any PII columns that must be removed at upload time (we can also accept encrypted columns).
4) If agreed, we’ll run the Redwood pilot using two model variants and share per‑model scoring + latency/cost breakdown within 3 business days of dataset receipt.

Recommended model candidates to start with (we'll tune after first run):
- redwood-instruct-13B-q4f16 (fast, lower cost, good for template-based summaries)
- redwood-chat-33B-qlora (higher quality for nuanced clinical language; expect higher latency)

Temporary note on QA/regression: we’ll run the pilot against the prompt set in prompt_set_v2.txt (attached) and evaluate using the scoring template (scoring_template.xlsx). We’ll flag any quality regressions relative to the human baseline and include per‑example diffs.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: you confirm dataset export format and PII constraints.
- Tue 2/22: you deliver ~1k de‑identified sample.
- Wed–Fri 2/23–2/25: Redwood runs pilot and returns scoring dashboard + raw outputs.

If that all looks good I’ll open the eval run and add Marissa as the ops owner for execution.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Next steps: Sienna Health pilot — evaluation datasets & scoring

Thanks Alex — really useful summary. Quick clarifications:

- We can produce a 1k sample but ask that PHI be redacted first. Will the sample need a consistent patient identifier (hashed id) to support per-patient grouping in scoring?
- For scoring: we want exact-match on medication names and discrete fields (severity level), but allow fuzzy matching for free-text summaries. Can you share the fuzzy scorer you use (is it embed-similarity or model-based scoring)?
- Latency: 600ms 95p is tight if we pick the 33B model; are you assuming the Dedicated environment? We’re evaluating hosted vs dedicated.

Also — is there a way to re-run only failed examples quickly (we have a few hundred long notes that might timeout)?

Luke
Luke Parker
Head of Clinical AI, Sienna Health
luke.parker@siennahealth.com

To: Luke Parker <luke.parker@siennahealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@siennahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Next steps: Sienna Health pilot — evaluation datasets & scoring

Appreciate the questions — answers and concrete ops below.

1) Identifiers: yes, please include a consistent hashed_patient_id field in the JSONL sample. That lets us compute per‑patient aggregation and prevent double-counting in the scorer.

2) Scoring approach:
- Discrete fields (meds, severity): we use token- and entity-level exact-match rules first. For minor normalization differences (e.g., acetaminophen vs. paracetamol) we provide a normalization table — you can add synonyms in the metadata column.
- Free-text summaries: we run a two-step score: (a) embedding similarity (Cosine) against gold summary, and (b) a model-based classification check for hallucination (binary: hallucination/no-hallucination). Both scores are combined into a weighted quality score column in scoring_template.xlsx. We’ll include per-example score breakdown and highlight hallucination candidates for human review.

3) Latency and deployment flavor:
- Hosted (Redwood API): redwood-instruct-13B-q4f16 will meet the 600ms 95p target for short notes in hosted mode with batching disabled and prefix cache warmed. redwood-chat-33B-qlora will likely be ~800–1200ms 95p hosted — if 95p <600ms is a hard requirement we recommend Dedicated capacity with 33B (we can provide estimated reserved throughput).
- For the pilot we suggest running both variants in hosted mode to collect quality delta and cost numbers; if latency is prohibitive we can re-run the 33B on Dedicated for a follow-up.

4) Timeouts / retries: Redwood eval runner supports per-example retries and an optional short-circuit for long notes. We can configure: max_tokens_per_example, per-example timeout (default 8s) and a retry limit (default 1). Failed items are exported to failed_examples.jsonl for quick re-run.

5) Ops instructions (what we’ll do once we have your sample):
- You upload sample to the secure eval bucket we’ll create (we’ll send a drive + signed upload link).
- We validate format against si_eval_sample.jsonl; if normalization table needed we’ll add synonyms.csv.
- We create two eval runs: run-A (13B q4f16) and run-B (33B qlora) using the provided prompt_set_v2.txt.
- We provide a scoring dashboard link and a CSV export of per-example scores.

6) Parameters I’ll set for the initial pilot (can tune after first run):
- batch_size: 8 for 13B, 4 for 33B
- temp: 0.0 for deterministic extraction tasks, 0.2 for triage suggestion tasks
- max_output_tokens: 256
- kv_cache_warmup: enabled for repeated patient examples

Attachments included: prompt_set_v2.txt (prompt templates), scoring_template.xlsx (scoring weightings and pass/fail thresholds).

Proposed adjusted timeline given the sample:
- Thu 2/19 EOD: you confirm hashed_id + PII redaction plan.
- Mon 2/22: you upload 1k sample to secure link.
- Tue 2/23–Thu 2/25: Redwood runs evals and we deliver scoring dashboard and raw outputs.

Let me know if you want us to include an explicit human baseline column — we can add a small 50-example manual annotation step for sanity checking.

Best — Alex

Attachments: prompt_set_v2.txt (text), scoring_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Marissa / Ben — looping you both in with the external thread above. Short asks:

1) Marissa — can you provision the secure eval bucket for Sienna (SIE-2027-004) and pre-create two eval runs with the parameter presets above? I’ll add the dataset once Luke uploads. Aim to have runs ready to trigger by Mon 2/22.

2) Ben — can you review the scoring_template.xlsx thresholds and confirm the hallucination classifier model (we talked about using hf/halluc-det-v1) — want to ensure it aligns with clinical tolerances. If you think a stricter threshold is needed for medications, propose exact-match fallbacks.

3) If either of you think we should start with a smaller human-baseline set (50 ex) let’s approve that now — I’ll offer to get Sienna a quick cost estimate for the manual annotation.

Thanks — Alex
